nodes.description: Fluoride disrupts iron handling in maturation-stage ameloblasts, with ferritin heavy chain emerging as a preferential molecular target. Reduced iron storage is associated with reduced iron oxides in enamel and altered enamel ultrastructure and mechanical properties.
nodes.id: Ameloblast iron storage and ferritin deficiency

evidence.reference_title: Disrupted Iron Storage in Dental Fluorosis.
evidence.snippet: Iron storage was drastically reduced by fluoride. Among the proteins involved in iron metabolism, ferritin heavy chain (Fth), in charge of iron storage, appeared as the preferential target of fluoride

evidence.reference_title: Disrupted Iron Storage in Dental Fluorosis.
evidence.snippet: Fluorotic enamel presented a decreased quantity of iron oxides attested by electron spin resonance technique, altered mechanical properties measured by nanoindentation, and ultrastructural defects analyzed by scanning electron microscopy

nodes.description: High intake of fluoride-rich brick tea infusion or buttered brick tea causes brick tea-type endemic dental fluorosis in Tibetan and western Chinese populations even where drinking water fluoride levels are low.

evidence.reference_title: Brick tea consumption and its relationship with fluorosis in Tibetan areas.
evidence.snippet: Brick tea-type fluorosis (BTF) due to a high intake of brick tea is possible in Tibetan populations, and dental fluorosis (DF) and skeletal fluorosis (SF) are its primary manifestations.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of Brick Tea-Type Fluorosis in the Tibet Autonomous Region.
evidence.snippet: The average daily fluoride intake from drinking brick tea in all seven districts in Tibet was much higher than the national standard. The prevalence of dental fluorosis was 33.57%

nodes.description: Dietary supplementation with calcium and vitamin D in conjunction with replacing high-fluoride drinking water restores elemental homeostasis and alleviates dental fluorosis severity in preclinical fluorosis models.

evidence.reference_title: Calcium and Vitamin D Supplementation Effectively Alleviates Dental and Skeletal Fluorosis and Retain Elemental Homeostasis in Mice.
evidence.snippet: Substitution of NaF-containing water with normal drinking water reduced the severity of fluorosis but supplementation of calcium and vitamin D effectively alleviated dental and skeletal fluorosis

nodes.description: Dental fluorosis arises when systemic fluoride exposure exceeds the narrow developmental tolerance of enamel-forming teeth during amelogenesis, especially during childhood tooth formation. Higher fluoride in drinking water is associated with sharply increased fluorosis risk, and children in actively growing developmental stages appear more vulnerable to retention of systemic fluoride in mineralizing tissues.

evidence.reference_title: Optimal fluoride concentration in drinking water for balancing dental caries prevention and fluorosis control in Jinan, China.
evidence.snippet: each 1 mg/L increase in fluoride concentration was associated with a 1,246% (OR: 13.46, 95%CI: 8.30, 21.84) increase in the risk of dental fluorosis

evidence.reference_title: Developmental vulnerability to fluoride toxicity: enamel and clearance differences in adolescent versus mature mice
evidence.snippet: These findings demonstrate that younger mice are more vulnerable to fluoride-induced enamel defects due to lower clearance than mature mice.

nodes.description: Engineering and public-health water improvement projects that replace high-fluoride water sources or defluoridate drinking water below 1.5 mg/L markedly reduce the incidence and severity of endemic dental fluorosis in children.
nodes.id: Drinking water defluoridation and water source improvement

evidence.reference_title: Effects of water improvement and defluoridation on fluorosis-endemic areas in China: A meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: With water improvement, water fluoride levels decreased from 2.72 mg/L to 0.54 mg/L (95% confidence intervals: -2.75, -1.58), which was below the standard for drinking water (1.5 mg/L). Additionally, after water improvement, the prevalence of dental fluorosis decreased from 54.5% to 36.2%

nodes.description: Early-life toothbrushing with fluoridated toothpaste during infancy and early childhood is an independent risk factor for dental fluorosis due to swallowing of toothpaste during active enamel formation.

nodes.description: Fluoride exposure and altered ameloblast calcium handling (including TRPM7, STIM proteins, and store-operated calcium entry) disrupt maturation-stage ameloblast modulation and mineralization.
